name: Mongolia
summary_text: Mongolia decriminalised consensual same-sex intimacy in 1993. Discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity is prohibited, but the protections are fragmented and no comprehensive equality law is in place. The constitution bars marriage equality, and no form of union recognition is available to same-sex couples. LGBT organisations can register.  The Criminal Code in force from 2017 carries hate-crime provisions covering bias motivated by sexual orientation and gender identity. A residual offence addressing "satisfaction of immoral sexual needs" remains in the statute book and can be invoked as a pretext against gender-nonconforming people, even though no provision specifically criminalises homosexuality.  Enforcement practice works in the visitor's favour. After a police officer was charged in 2019 for assaulting a detained transgender woman, the LGBT Centre trained more than 500 police officers, prosecutors and judges on the 2017 Criminal Code's hate-crime provisions. The force now has guidelines requiring officers to address transgender detainees by their identified gender regardless of what identity documents say.  Transition and visibility remain difficult in practice. An openly trans man, Anaraa Nyamdorj, co-founder and advisor of the LGBT Centre, came out publicly in 2004 and began transition in 2011; his account and the Centre's advocacy describe limited access to transition-related care and uneven social acceptance in Ulaanbaatar. Mongolia held its first Pride in 2018.

name: Northern Mariana Islands
summary_text: The Northern Mariana Islands is a US commonwealth and stands under the national framework of the United States for travel documents, immigration and airport screening. United States passports and entry documents reflect sex assigned at birth, and the X marker option was eliminated by the January 2025 executive order, so a trans visitor travelling on United States documents presents a gender marker that may not match presentation at the port of entry.  Screening at the airport follows federal procedure, and the order halting federal funding for gender-affirming care reaches federally funded institutions in the territory, so access to such care during a visit cannot be assumed. In February 2025 the United States State Department additionally announced visa denials for trans athletes seeking entry to compete in women's sports.  Consensual same-sex conduct is not criminalised, and same-sex marriage has been legal since 2015 under Obergefell v. Hodges; the first same-sex marriage on Saipan was officiated on 27 July 2015. Adoption has been available to same-sex couples since 2015.  Commonwealth law provides for enhanced sentencing in hate-motivated crimes: CNMI Public Law 22-32, signed in January 2023, amends the Commonwealth Code with criteria covering offences motivated by sexual orientation and gender identity. This is the principal commonwealth-level protection with direct bearing on gender-identity-motivated violence.  Legal gender change is permitted in the Northern Mariana Islands provided the applicant has undergone the specified medical process, which means identity documents can be brought into line with presentation, subject to that medical requirement.  Wider protection remains thin. As of 27 September 2026 the Movement Advancement Project scored the territory's sexual orientation policy at 3.5 of 22 and its gender identity policy at minus 2 of 25, an overall rating of 1.5 of 47, classified as Low with a Negative gender-identity score. There is no comprehensive commonwealth nondiscrimination statute covering gender identity; recourse beyond federal EEOC complaint channels is limited, and commonwealth-level protections extend to government employees only.
